## SC26: Trends from the Frontier of Agentic AI in the Enterprise


Garrett VanLee


November 23, 2026


Supercomputing 2026 brought the HPC and scientific computing community to Chicago to compare the systems, software, and methods shaping the next phase of technical computing. Across the exhibit floor, partner stages, and technical sessions, the topics focused on how organizations will turn new AI capabilities and scarce compute resources into useful scientific and engineering work. For many organizations, available capacity is struggling to keep up with their surging demand. So engineering and technology decision makers were on the hunt for new architectures, procurement models, and workflow optimizations to get more output from every compute cycle.


This year “agentic” was no longer the nascent concept it was just a year prior at SC25. It appeared across scientific computing, high performance computing (HPC), electronic design automation, and simulation. Demonstrations showed agents writing code, configuring workloads, optimizing algorithms, troubleshooting failures, and coordinating multiple tools. The shift is meaningful for engineering organizations because it moves the conversation beyond whether AI can answer a question. The question now is whether an agent can help move a product-development workflow forward, with the context, controls, and evidence that engineering decisions require.


Scaling compute is absolutely necessary, but on its own it does not solve many of the emergent problems of deploying engineering agents in production workflows. The durable agentic advantage comes from connecting engineering knowledge, simulation methods, AI, and infrastructure into workflows that teams can understand, govern, and improve over time. That is the same direction behind[Rescale’s Fall 2026 Showcase](https://rescale.com/lp/fall-2026-product-showcase/) and the three themes we brought to SC26: Agentic digital engineering, AI physics, and compute orchestration. Across the Rescale booth, partner stages, and customer conversations, those themes gave us a practical way to discuss what it takes to move from an impressive demo to repeatable engineering work.


*HPC and AI panel kicked off the week covering the state of the industry including supply chain constraints to how workflows are evolving to incorporate agents.*


## When Workflow Reigns Supreme, Context and Compute Follow

The clearest signal from SC26 was not that every vendor had an agent. It was that the stack is being reorganized around workflows: agents need domain knowledge, validated tools, appropriate compute, and a way to check their work before results inform decisions. That shift was visible in both compute and data platforms, where new capabilities are giving agents richer context, validated tools, and better access to the infrastructure and information they need to plan, execute, and evaluate work.


Across the event, numerous ecosystem announcements reinforced the importance of workflows as the reason for technology advancement.[NVIDIA’s SC26 overview](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ian-buck-sc26/) described scientific agents that plan experiments, select tools, run simulations, and evaluate results, alongside Nemotron for Science and Rubin HPC.[Google Cloud’s SC26 update](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/hpc/whats-new-in-hpc-and-ai-at-sc26) paired reusable agent skills with Cluster Toolkit blueprints, domain workloads, and evolutionary optimization. Microsoft Discovery presented a similar R&D direction, organizing data, tools, models, and compute around complex discovery tasks.


The infrastructure story is also changing, from static compute capacity to dynamic systems that can adapt to agent-driven workloads.[AMD’s SC26 update](https://newsroom.amd.com/news/sc26-amd-expands-frontier-scientific-computing/) connected CPUs, GPUs, networking, and open software in heterogeneous systems, while agentic orchestration adds configuration guidance into job submission, profiling, and optimization. AWS and Rescale’s SC26 demonstrations likewise emphasized elastic infrastructure and operational controls for agentic digital engineering, AI physics, and HPC workloads. Synopsys showed how AI is moving into engineering design and verification, with examples a mix of applications.


When added together, these developments support a clear perspective Rescale has long held: no single model, accelerator, cloud, or engineering application is the complete answer for R&D organizations. The value comes from coordinating those layers around the work engineers need to complete. That means grounding agents in engineering data, connecting them to the applications and workflows where decisions happen, and managing the compute, permissions, and verification steps that keep execution reliable.


For engineering and R&D leaders, this creates both opportunity and pressure. The organizations that benefit will be the ones that can turn a growing set of models, skills, applications, and infrastructure choices into a repeatable operating model rather than another collection of disconnected point tools.


*AI-driven engineering was a key topic discussed among industry practitioners focused on integrating AI and agentic workflows to drive exploration and validation loops.*


## What it Takes to Put Agents to Work in Engineering


The most important lesson from SC26 was that an agent’s value depends on what it knows, what it can access, and what it is allowed to do. A general-purpose model may generate a plausible answer, but product development depends on program standards, solver conventions, acceptance criteria, local tools, historical results, and the judgment of experienced engineers.


The AWS SimPossible booth demonstrations made that idea concrete. Agents started with science and engineering objectives expressed in natural language, then worked through requirements in iterative loops, selecting tools, refining the task, and moving toward an executable result. The point was not a one-shot answer, but a process that lets experts guide and verify the work as it develops.


That is why the[Fall Showcase](https://rescale.com/lp/fall-2026-product-showcase/) positions agentic digital engineering as an engineering-specific harness. Rescale’s[Agentic Projects](https://rescale.com/release-notes/agentic-projects-for-project-knowledge-that-carries-across-sessions-and-teams/) allows teams to define the objectives, skills, tools, and guardrails an agent uses. Project memory retains learnings that engineers explicitly approve, and a[gent nodes](https://rescale.com/release-notes/edison-node-custom-ai-steps-in-your-workflows/) add agent-driven steps such as validating inputs, analyzing results, or preparing evidence. Engineers remain in control of actions and approvals, while teams can save and share the methods that make a workflow repeatable.


*Rescale booth visitors were interested to learn how they can quickly integrate all the innovations seen across the event from the latest computing infrastructure to agentic harness capabilities.*


[Engineering intelligence](https://rescale.com/release-notes/engineering-context-agents-that-answer-from-your-standards-your-data-and-your-prior-runs/) provides the context layer beneath those workflows. By connecting requirements, design, simulation, test, and process data, knowledge graphs give agents access to the relationships behind an engineering decision.[Rescale Desktop](https://docs.rescale.com/release-notes/rescale-desktop-app) extends that experience to local files, desktop applications, and on-premises resources.[Expanded MCP connectivity](https://rescale.com/release-notes/use-rescale-agents-from-claude-chatgpt-and-other-ai-assistants/) makes it possible to bring Rescale context and actions into tools engineers already use.


Even with MCP integrations into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, the agentic workflow is more than submitting a request to an off-the-shelf model or tool. It requires capturing the state and intent behind each step, carrying that context forward, and checking results against trusted engineering baselines before the work advances.


This is the difference between an agent that completes a task once and an agentic workflow that becomes more useful with every program. The objective is not to remove engineering judgment. It is to apply that judgment where it matters most, while reducing the configuration, troubleshooting, documentation, and handoff work that slows teams down.


## AI Inference Engineering Use Cases Expand


At SC26, inference computing has continued to expand as a critical workload requirement. Seen in ubiquitous “AI factory” messaging throughout the event, infrastructure and software providers added capacity and capabilities that support AI inference across generative AI, agent execution, scientific workloads, and engineering applications. These use cases are starting to converge: the same underlying data movement, model-serving, orchestration, and performance concerns determine whether an AI system can move from a demonstration to a production workflow.


For engineering organizations, AI physics is one expression of this broader inference opportunity. The challenge is not only to train a surrogate model, but to build the data pipelines and agent workflows around it: identify and prepare simulation data, create training sets, tune models, evaluate confidence, trigger retraining as new results arrive, and route uncertain predictions to full-fidelity simulation. That workflow turns inference into a repeatable engineering capability.


Rescale’s AI physics capabilities are designed around this production path.[Agentic dataset creation](https://docs.rescale.com/release-notes/dataset-creation-agent) and[guided preprocessing](https://docs.rescale.com/release-notes/guided-preprocessing) help teams prepare data from existing simulation work.[Auto Tune](https://rescale.com/release-notes/ai-physics-auto-tune-for-faster-better-surrogate-model-training/) reduces manual model configuration.[Design Explorer](https://rescale.com/release-notes/explore-and-optimize-multi-physics-design-spaces-with-ai-physics/) brings surrogate predictions into design decisions, while[uncertainty and out-of-distribution signals](https://rescale.com/release-notes/uncertainty-quantification-for-ai-physics-know-when-to-trust-your-surrogate-predictions/) show when to trust a result, improve the model, or run a full simulation. Agent-driven workflows can connect these steps into repeatable pipelines, enabling teams to generate, validate, and maintain production-grade AI physics models without separating model development from engineering work.


*Rescale’s presentation at the Microsoft Innovation Theater demonstrated how digital twins are transforming manufacturing using live simulation predictions from AI physics surrogate models.*


The broader SC26 message was that inference will be embedded in many workflows, not confined to a single model or infrastructure configuration. For R&D teams, the opportunity is to treat inference as part of the engineering system, with the data, agents, applications, and compute needed to use models responsibly and at scale.


## Compute Orchestration Turns Capacity Into Throughput


Agents change the operating profile of HPC by creating more dynamic, iterative workloads that move across compute, storage, and software resources. They can submit more work, run longer campaigns, create new data, and shift between CPU, GPU, storage, and application resources. As demand grows and capacity remains constrained, every wasted run or poorly placed workload carries a larger cost in time and opportunity. In that environment, leaders need more than access to infrastructure. They need visibility into how work is executing and controls for directing resources toward the highest-value outcomes.


Rescale’s compute orchestration capabilities address that operating layer by helping teams see where work slows, prioritize jobs, and make better decisions about how and where workloads run.[Cluster performance metrics](https://rescale.com/release-notes/cluster-performance-metrics-generally-available/) show where execution slows and why jobs are waiting.[Priority score](https://rescale.com/release-notes/priority-score-early-access-beta/) provides a predictable way to order work using factors such as wait time, job size, and resource usage.[Compute economics controls](https://docs.rescale.com/release-notes/new-commitment-burst-policy-economy) help teams decide when work should wait, burst, or use an alternate resource path.


*Novel computing architectures supporting a range of high performance computing and AI workloads were introduced, including NVIDIAs Rubin HPC GPU.*


The goal is to make compute execution visible and policy-driven. For R&D leaders, that means greater confidence that agentic workflows can scale without turning cost and throughput into unknowns. For HPC and AI decision makers, it creates a way to evaluate infrastructure based on the engineering work it enables, not only on peak hardware specifications.


## What This Year’s Trends Mean for Engineering Leaders


SC26 made the direction of the market clear: engineering AI is becoming an execution problem, not just a model problem. NVIDIA, Google Cloud, Microsoft, AMD, AWS, and engineering software providers are each advancing important parts of an AI-enabled scientific and engineering stack. The next challenge is integration: connecting agents to the right data, methods, applications, and compute while preserving governance and verification.


That is where Rescale is focused. The digital engineering platform for the AI era brings the workflow, context, AI methods, and infrastructure together so engineering organizations can move from demonstrations to repeatable operating capability.
